question: Can a windowed-photometry LM polish (free omega, fit predicted-observed magnitude over a forward window) break the s105 hard-shoot trap and reach Band A on fast-tumbler seed 119?
hypothesis: Replacing the hard A->B connection with a photometry-objective polish over a forward window pulls the seed omega from Band D into Band A.
narrative_md: Windowed-photometry LM polish (free omega, minimize predicted-observed mag over a forward A->C window, seeded from the pair-shoot root) breaks the s105 hard-shoot trap on seed 119's near-truth cloud pair: 0.687/Band D/4.25-deg-off -> 0.0300/Band A/0.57-deg-off, |omega| 1.5025 deg/s -- first Band A on this fast tumbler. Two findings: the soft B-attitude term is inert (w_B 0/0.1/1.0 identical); the window choice is the lever (abc->A, full-LC->D 32 deg, narrow-C->D 151 deg). Seeded from the ORACLE-NEAREST pair, q_a held at truth-nearest rep (oracle-leak); discrimination/generalization untested, N=1.
